newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate climbs further to 9.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate climbs further to 9.4 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average lending rate climbed further to 9.4 percent on Wednesday from 9.2 percent due to stronger demand for kuna, money market dealers said.
They said interbank borrowings were made at 9.0-12 percent. Insurers charged a steady 8.0 percent on their short-term placements.

Wednesday's supply, totalling 54.5 million kuna after some banks invested into central bank bills, was completely mopped up. The trade left a shortfall of some 16 million as one bank sought to repay a Lombard loan to the National Bank.
Due to a mandatory reserve payment, overnight loans on Wednesday rose slightly to 88.7 million kuna.
The central bank quoted kuna midrates for Thursday weaker at 5.4861 to the dollar and to 3.5631 against the mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
